project: Core File Module And Tool Executable Reorganization
goal: Introduce one Core-owned file module for native file dialog and file-runtime utilities, and reorganize engine tools under a dedicated tool executable level. Profiler becomes the first tool executable under that level, so future tools can follow the same source-tree and CMake entry pattern without changing runtime layering.

direct_call_sites.detail: Scene selection UI directly includes nfd.hpp and calls NFD::OpenDialog from the Config window. The UI layer owns both dialog invocation and result application.
Profiler CSV loading directly includes nfd.hpp and calls NFD::OpenDialog from profiler UI code.

ownership_gap.detail: Engine owns editor runtime systems, but file dialog capability is not owned by a Core runtime utility. Remaining dialog calls stay in UI code.
Profiler does not run under Engine, so any file dialog capability that only exists in Engine would duplicate ownership and break reuse.

organization_gap.detail: Profiler is still added as a special top-level executable entry. There is no dedicated tool executable level in the source tree.
Profiler target exists directly under source/profiler instead of being organized under a tool executable entry such as source/tool/profiler.

build_graph_issues.detail: Editor links nfd directly, which leaks third-party ownership to the app layer.
Moer::Render currently links nfd publicly even though the visible dialog use sites are editor and profiler UI concerns. This is the wrong dependency owner for a Core file capability.
Profiler does not link nfd explicitly and only gets it transitively through runtime targets, which hides the real ownership boundary.

hard_constraints.title: Tool is executable-level organization only
hard_constraints.detail: Tool is not a runtime peer layer of Render. It only represents the source-tree and CMake organization level for engine tool executables.

hard_constraints.title: Core owns file capability
hard_constraints.detail: The file module must live under runtime/core so both editor runtime and tool executables can reuse it. Do not place the concrete dialog implementation inside Engine, EditorUI, Profiler UI, or Render-only code.

hard_constraints.title: Profiler becomes the first tool executable
hard_constraints.detail: Profiler should be reorganized under the tool executable level so future tools can follow the same entry pattern instead of becoming new top-level special cases.

hard_constraints.title: No direct third-party dialog calls outside Core
hard_constraints.detail: After migration, EditorUI and profiler UI code must not include nfd.hpp or call NFD APIs directly. All native dialog interaction goes through one repo-owned Core API.

hard_constraints.title: Public API must not leak third-party types
hard_constraints.detail: Core public headers must expose repo-owned request, filter, and result types only. Do not return or accept NFD-specific structs, enums, or ownership wrappers from public APIs.

hard_constraints.title: Bootstrap remains explicit
hard_constraints.detail: Editor runtime may bootstrap file capability from Engine, while tool executables bootstrap shared services from their own executable entry. The Core file module itself must not depend on Engine being present.

hard_constraints.title: Main-thread dialog rule
hard_constraints.detail: Native open or save dialogs are treated as main-thread runtime operations in the first landing. Do not design an async worker-thread dialog model.

hard_constraints.title: Latest-only path
hard_constraints.detail: Do not keep mixed usage where some UI code still calls NFD directly while new code uses Core, and do not keep profiler both as a top-level executable entry and as a tool executable entry. The migration target is one path only.

layering.runtime: Runtime layering remains centered on Core and Render. This checkpoint does not introduce a new runtime peer layer named Tool.
layering.tool_level: Tool is a source-tree and executable-entry organization level under source/tool for engine tool executables.

ownership_model.core_file_module: Owns request and result types, backend lifecycle, third-party integration, and narrow native dialog entry points.
ownership_model.engine: Bootstraps file capability for the editor application only. Engine remains the editor runtime owner, but it is not the canonical home of the file-dialog backend.
ownership_model.tool_executables: Tool executables are organized under source/tool and bootstrap their own application entry while consuming Core capabilities directly.
ownership_model.profiler: Becomes the first concrete tool executable under source/tool/profiler and consumes Core file capability instead of direct third-party calls.
ownership_model.ui_layers: Editor UI and profiler UI become request producers and result consumers only. They do not own native dialog lifecycle or backend headers.

must_include: Optional save file dialog if implementation wants a symmetric minimal API
Dialog filter description owned by repo types
Path result object using std::filesystem::path or a repo-owned wrapper around it
Tool executable organization with profiler as the first entry
should_not_include: A new runtime peer layer named tool

principles: Keep the API narrow and operation-oriented.
Expose semantic request structs instead of raw third-party argument lists.
Return explicit status such as success, cancel, or failure plus path payload when applicable.

consumer_examples.current_behavior: UI directly opens a dialog and mutates scene_path.
consumer_examples.target_behavior: UI requests an open-file operation from the Core file module, then applies the returned path to scene_path and reload state.

consumer_examples.current_behavior: Profiler UI directly opens a dialog and loads CSV on success.
consumer_examples.target_behavior: Profiler UI requests an open-file operation from the same Core module and loads the returned path on success.

checkpoints.title: Introduce the tool executable level
checkpoints.problem: Profiler is still a special top-level executable entry and there is no dedicated tool executable level for future tools.
must_be_true_after: A source/tool executable level exists.
Profiler is organized as the first tool executable entry.
Future tools can follow the same source-tree and CMake pattern.
tasks: Define the tool executable level under source/tool.
Move profiler target registration under source/tool/profiler.
Remove the need for a special top-level source/profiler executable entry.

checkpoints.title: Freeze the Core file-module boundary
checkpoints.problem: Dialog capability currently lives in UI code and third-party headers leak into consumers. There is no single repo-owned file-module boundary.
must_be_true_after: One Core-owned module defines dialog request, filter, and result types.
Public APIs expose no NFD-specific types.
The module location and ownership are explicit in the architecture.
tasks: Define the public folder and namespace for the module under runtime/core.
Define repo-owned request and result structs.
Define the minimal first-landing operation set and reject broader speculative file-service design.

checkpoints.title: Define editor and tool-executable bootstrap ownership
checkpoints.problem: Editor runtime and tool executables have different entry shapes. A design that only fits Engine would force profiler and later tools into the wrong ownership path.
must_be_true_after: Editor bootstraps the file module from Engine-owned runtime lifetime.
Tool executables bootstrap their own app entry and consume Core capabilities directly.
The Core file module itself does not depend on Engine being present.
tasks: Define the Engine-side bootstrap point for the editor executable.
Define the tool-executable bootstrap point for profiler-like tools.
State the main-thread ownership rule for all dialog operations.

checkpoints.title: Move editor and profiler consumers to semantic file requests
checkpoints.problem: UI layers currently own raw dialog calls. That keeps third-party APIs in user-facing code and mixes UI intent with backend details.
must_be_true_after: EditorUI no longer includes nfd.hpp or calls NFD APIs directly.
Profiler UI no longer includes nfd.hpp or calls NFD APIs directly.
Consumers request file operations semantically and handle only repo-owned results.
tasks: Replace scene open flow with a Core file-module request.
Replace profiler CSV browse flow with the same Core file-module request path.
Delete direct NFD error handling from consumer code after migration.

checkpoints.title: Fix dependency and CMake ownership
checkpoints.problem: The current build graph hides real ownership and leaks nfd through the wrong layer.
must_be_true_after: The concrete native dialog backend is linked where the Core implementation lives, not through Render as a public dependency.
Editor and tool executables get the capability through the Core or runtime targets they already depend on.
Moer::Render no longer owns nfd unless a real render-side usage remains.
Top-level source/CMake layout reflects the tool executable level instead of a special profiler entry.
tasks: Move backend linkage to the Core implementation owner.
Remove public nfd leakage from runtime/render if no remaining render-side implementation needs it.
Keep executable target linkage minimal after the Core file module exists.

checkpoints.title: Keep the file module and tool executable level narrow
checkpoints.problem: A new Core file module plus tool executable level can easily bloat into a generic filesystem framework or a generic tool-plugin architecture that the current problem does not require.
must_be_true_after: The first landing solves native open or save dialog access and minimal path-oriented file request types only.
The file module does not introduce virtual filesystem abstractions, async job systems, or plugin registries.
The tool executable level remains a source-tree and CMake organization concept, not a fake runtime framework.
Ownership stays explicit and readable.
tasks: Reject wrapper layers that only rename NFD calls without owning a real invariant.
Keep dialog operations synchronous and main-thread only in the first landing.
Keep tool-level structure to the minimum needed for profiler and the next real tool.

milestones.title: Freeze executable organization first
milestones.why: Without freezing the tool executable level first, profiler remains a special case and future tools still have no clean entry pattern.

milestones.title: Freeze Core file boundary and bootstrap rules
milestones.why: After the executable-level organization is fixed, the file capability boundary and editor-vs-tool bootstrap rules can stay clean and reusable.

milestones.title: Migrate consumers and fix the build graph
milestones.why: The architecture only becomes real when editor and profiler stop calling NFD directly and the ownership change is visible in CMake.

milestones.title: Lock scope and validation contract
milestones.why: This prevents the file module and tool executable level from turning into broad frameworks without a concrete second tool driving the design.

design_notes.tool_rule: Tool is only the engine tool executable level. It changes source-tree and CMake organization, not runtime layering.
design_notes.profiler_rule: Profiler should become the first tool executable entry and define the pattern future tools follow. Keeping profiler as a one-off top-level executable weakens the organization model.
design_notes.module_rule: File dialog capability is a runtime utility, but its implementation home should be Core because both editor runtime and tool executables need it. Engine is one bootstrapper, not the global owner of the feature.
design_notes.ui_rule: UI code should express intent such as scene-open or csv-browse, then consume a repo-owned path result. UI code should not own third-party dialog calls.
design_notes.dependency_rule: Third-party dialog backends should be linked by the Core implementation target and hidden from public headers. Render should not own that dependency.
design_notes.scope_rule: Do not turn this into a generic filesystem framework or a generic tool-plugin architecture. Solve the file capability and the profiler-as-first-tool executable pattern first.

risks: If profiler is not moved under a real tool executable level, future tools will keep becoming one-off executable entries and the source tree will continue to fragment.
If the dialog implementation is put directly in Engine, tool executables will either duplicate the feature or create a bad dependency on editor runtime.
If the public Core API leaks NFD types, the repository will remain coupled to that backend and future replacement cost will stay high.
If Moer::Render keeps public ownership of nfd, the build graph will continue to hide the real dependency boundary.
If the module scope is left vague, this work can bloat into a generic file framework instead of solving the concrete dialog problem.
validation: Planning plus organization changes only in this checkpoint update.
When implementation starts, validate with existing repository build and test scripts only.
Run powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\testscripts\test_all.ps1 after implementation-sized changes.
State explicitly that native dialog interaction is not covered by current automation and still requires manual runtime verification unless existing scripts are extended.
If profiler executable reorganization changes target layout, document any remaining manual profiler runtime checks instead of adding a new top-level test harness.
